q: What does a men's Olympic javelin weigh?
hint: For scale: a baseball weighs about {0.145 kg}.
card: The javelin was redesigned in 1986 after East Germany's Uwe Hohn threw one more than {104 m}, dangerously close to the crowd.
clue: A regulation basketball weighs about {0.62 kg}.

q: How long is the swim in a full Ironman triathlon?
hint: For scale: an Olympic swimming pool is {50 m} long.
card: The Ironman distances came from three Hawaii races: the Waikiki swim, a bike ride around Oahu and the Honolulu Marathon.
clue: The swim in an Olympic-distance triathlon is {1.5 km}.

q: How long is a regulation table tennis table?
hint: For scale: a tennis court is about {24 m} long.
card: Table tennis balls grew from {38 mm} to {40 mm} across in 2000, partly to slow rallies down for TV viewers.
clue: A king-size bed is about {2 m} long.

q: In what year did Roger Bannister run the first mile in under four minutes?
hint: For scale: the first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896.
card: Bannister ran 3:59.4 at Oxford, and his record lasted just 46 days before Australia's John Landy beat it.
clue: Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the Berlin Olympics in 1936.

q: What is the most a regulation golf ball is allowed to weigh?
hint: For scale: a ping-pong ball weighs about {0.0027 kg}.
card: Dimples help a golf ball fly farther by cutting the drag that slows a smooth ball.
clue: A tennis ball weighs about {0.058 kg}.

q: How many players does each water polo team have in the water, goalkeeper included?
hint: For scale: a soccer team fields 11 players.
card: Field players aren't allowed to touch the bottom of the pool, so they tread water for the whole game.
clue: A volleyball team has 6 players on the court.

q: How long is one lap of an Olympic track-cycling velodrome?
hint: For scale: an Olympic swimming pool is {50 m} long.
card: Velodrome tracks are steeply banked on the turns, tilting at up to about 45 degrees.
clue: One lap of a standard running track's inside lane is {400 m}.

q: How many episodes of HBO's The Wire were made?
hint: For scale: a typical US network drama season has about 22 episodes.
card: Creator David Simon had been a Baltimore Sun crime reporter, and many characters were based on people he met.
clue: The Sopranos ran for 86 episodes.

q: How long is the original Star Wars (1977), in minutes?
hint: For scale: a sitcom episode runs about 22 minutes.
card: James Earl Jones, the voice of Darth Vader, went uncredited in the film's original release.
clue: A soccer match lasts 90 minutes plus stoppage time.

q: How many episodes of the sitcom Cheers were made?
hint: For scale: Breaking Bad made 62 episodes.
card: The bar's exterior was Boston's Bull & Finch Pub, which later renamed itself Cheers Beacon Hill.
clue: Seinfeld made 180 episodes.

q: In what year was Steven Spielberg's Jaws released?
hint: For scale: The Wizard of Oz came out in 1939.
card: The mechanical shark kept breaking down, so Spielberg showed it far less than planned, which made the film scarier.
clue: 2001: A Space Odyssey premiered in 1968.

q: How long is The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (2003), in minutes?
hint: For scale: a soccer match lasts 90 minutes.
card: It won all 11 Oscars it was nominated for, including Best Picture.
clue: Avengers: Endgame runs 181 minutes.

q: How tall is an Oscar statuette?
hint: For scale: a standard soda can is about {12 cm} tall.
card: During World War II, Oscars were made of painted plaster because metal was scarce.
clue: An official NFL football is about {28 cm} long.

q: How many episodes of The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air were made?
hint: For scale: a typical network sitcom season has about 24 episodes.
card: Will Smith performed the theme song, which tells how his character moved from West Philadelphia to Bel-Air.
clue: How I Met Your Mother made 208 episodes.

q: In what year did the Beatles release Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band?
hint: For scale: MTV launched in 1981.
card: The cover's crowd of cardboard cutouts includes Marilyn Monroe, Bob Dylan and Edgar Allan Poe.
clue: The Beatles released their first single, “Love Me Do,” in 1962.

q: In what year was Elvis Presley born?
hint: For scale: the Beatles' first single came out in 1962.
card: Elvis never performed a concert outside North America; his only shows abroad were in Canada.
clue: Chuck Berry was born in 1926.

q: How many semitones are in one octave?
hint: For scale: a standard piano has 88 keys.
card: Each semitone step raises the pitch by about 6%, so twelve of them exactly double it.
clue: A standard guitar has 6 strings.

q: How many performances did the original Broadway run of Cats play?
hint: For scale: a show playing eight times a week for a year gives about 400 performances.
card: Its lyrics come almost entirely from T. S. Eliot's 1939 poetry book Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats.
clue: The Phantom of the Opera's first Broadway run lasted about 35 years.

q: How many pedals does a typical American grand piano have?
hint: For scale: a big church organ has dozens of foot pedals.
card: The right-hand pedal lifts every damper off the strings, so notes keep ringing after you let go of the keys.
clue: A bicycle has 2 pedals.

q: In what year did the Rolling Stones release “(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction”?
hint: For scale: MTV launched in 1981.
card: Keith Richards said he came up with the riff in his sleep and woke to find it on his cassette recorder.
clue: Elvis Presley's “Heartbreak Hotel” came out in 1956.

q: How many strings does a standard mandolin have?
hint: For scale: a concert harp has 47 strings.
card: A mandolin is tuned like a violin, so violinists can pick one up with little practice.
clue: A standard guitar has 6 strings.

q: How many cards are in a standard tarot deck?
hint: For scale: a poker hand has 5 cards.
card: Tarot cards were first used in 15th-century Italy to play a trick-taking card game, long before fortune-telling.
clue: A standard deck of playing cards has 52 cards.

q: How many checkers does each player start with in backgammon?
hint: For scale: a deck of playing cards has 52 cards.
card: Backgammon is one of the oldest board games; a board about 5,000 years old was found in Iran's Burnt City.
clue: A soccer team fields 11 players.

q: How many cards is each player dealt at the start of a game of Uno?
hint: For scale: in bridge, each player is dealt 13 cards.
card: Uno was invented in 1971 by Merle Robbins, an Ohio barber, after an argument with his son over the rules of Crazy Eights.
clue: A poker hand has 5 cards.

q: In what year did the Slinky go on sale?
hint: For scale: the first Barbie doll went on sale in 1959.
card: Engineer Richard James got the idea when a torsion spring fell off a shelf and kept moving.
clue: Silly Putty was first sold as a toy in 1950.

q: In what year was the Tamagotchi virtual pet first released in Japan?
hint: For scale: Pac-Man hit arcades in 1980.
card: Its name blends the Japanese word for egg, tamago, with the English word watch.
clue: The Super Nintendo came out in Japan in 1990.

q: In what year did Nutella first go on sale?
hint: For scale: Oreo cookies were first sold in 1912.
card: It grew out of a sliceable hazelnut paste made by Pietro Ferrero in postwar Italy, when cocoa was scarce.
clue: Kinder Surprise eggs first went on sale in 1974.

q: In what year did Nintendo release the Famicom, the console the West knew as the NES, in Japan?
hint: For scale: the Magnavox Odyssey, the first home console, came out in 1972.
card: Famicom is short for Family Computer, and the first consoles were red and white.
clue: Nintendo's Game Boy came out in 1989.

q: How tall are the two front towers of Notre-Dame de Paris?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.
card: After the 2019 fire, the cathedral was restored and reopened in December 2024.
clue: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is about {56 m} tall.

q: How long is Switzerland's Gotthard Base Tunnel, the world's longest railway tunnel?
hint: For scale: Manhattan is about {21 km} long.
card: It opened in 2016 after 17 years of work, letting trains cross the Alps without climbing.
clue: The Channel Tunnel is about {50 km} long.

q: How tall is the Strat (formerly the Stratosphere) tower in Las Vegas?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty is about {93 m} tall to the torch.
card: It is the tallest freestanding observation tower in the United States, with thrill rides at the top.
clue: Seattle's Space Needle is about {184 m} tall.

q: How tall is the Berlin TV Tower (Fernsehturm) at Alexanderplatz?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty is about {93 m} tall to the torch.
card: When sunlight hits its steel sphere, a cross-shaped glint appears, which Berliners nicknamed the Pope's Revenge.
clue: The Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.

q: How tall is China's Three Gorges Dam?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It is the world's largest power station by installed capacity.
clue: The Hoover Dam is about {221 m} tall.

q: How long is the Hall of Mirrors in the Palace of Versailles?
hint: For scale: a tennis court is about {24 m} long.
card: The treaty that formally ended World War I was signed in the hall in 1919.
clue: An American football field is about {91 m} between the goal lines.

q: In what year did the glass pyramid at the Louvre in Paris open?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889.
card: Its architect, I. M. Pei, used 673 glass panes; the rumor that there are exactly 666 is a myth.
clue: The Pompidou art museum in Paris opened in 1977.

q: What is the diameter of Mercury?
hint: For scale: Earth is about {12,742 km} across.
card: Mercury is smaller than Jupiter's moon Ganymede, though it is about twice as massive.
clue: The Moon is about {3,475 km} across.

q: In what year did William Herschel discover the planet Uranus?
hint: For scale: Isaac Newton published his laws of motion in 1687.
card: Herschel first thought it was a comet, and wanted to name it George's Star after King George III.
clue: Captain Cook reached the east coast of Australia in 1770.

q: In what year did Valentina Tereshkova become the first woman in space?
hint: For scale: the Wright brothers first flew in 1903.
card: She orbited Earth 48 times in nearly three days, and remains the only woman to have flown solo in space.
clue: Sputnik 1 launched in 1957.

q: How fast does the Moon travel along its orbit around Earth?
hint: For scale: sound travels through air at about {343 m/s}.
card: The Moon drifts about {3.8 cm} farther from Earth every year.
clue: A rifle bullet can leave the barrel at about {900 m/s}.

q: How far is Jupiter from the Sun, on average?
hint: For scale: Earth is about {150,000,000 km} from the Sun.
card: Sunlight takes about 43 minutes to reach Jupiter, compared with about eight minutes to reach Earth.
clue: Saturn averages about {1,430,000,000 km} from the Sun.

q: How far from Earth does the James Webb Space Telescope orbit?
hint: For scale: the Moon is about {384,400 km} from Earth.
card: Webb's sunshield is about the size of a tennis court and has five layers, each thinner than a human hair.
clue: The Moon's path around Earth is about {2,400,000 km} long.

q: How wide is Saturn, measured across its equator?
hint: For scale: Earth is about {12,742 km} across.
card: Saturn is less dense than water, so in a big enough bathtub it would float.
clue: Jupiter is about {143,000 km} across at the equator.

q: How tall is an adult emperor penguin?
hint: For scale: a standard kitchen counter is about {90 cm} high.
card: Emperor penguins breed in the Antarctic winter, and the fathers balance the egg on their feet for about two months.
clue: A typical 7-year-old child is about {120 cm} tall.

q: How much does a typical full-term newborn baby weigh?
hint: For scale: a bag of sugar weighs about {1 kg}.
card: Newborns usually lose a little weight in their first days and regain it within about two weeks.
clue: A typical house cat weighs about {4.5 kg}.

q: How long is the adult human large intestine?
hint: For scale: a sheet of letter paper is about {28 cm} long.
card: The small intestine is several times longer; it's called small only because it is narrower.
clue: A standard interior door is about {2 m} tall.

q: How long can a male narwhal's tusk grow?
hint: For scale: an adult human is about {1.7 m} tall.
card: The narwhal's tusk is actually a tooth: a canine that spirals out through its upper lip.
clue: A king-size bed is about {2 m} long.

q: How much does a blue whale's heart weigh?
hint: For scale: an adult man weighs about {80 kg}.
card: A blue whale's heartbeat can drop to just two beats a minute on a deep dive.
clue: A grand piano weighs about {450 kg}.

q: In what year was the Human Genome Project declared complete?
hint: For scale: the double helix structure of DNA was published in 1953.
card: The project took 13 years and finished in April 2003, 50 years after the double helix was described.
clue: Dolly the sheep was born in 1996.

q: How many tiny bones are in the middle of each human ear?
hint: For scale: one human hand, wrist included, has 27 bones.
card: The stirrup, or stapes, is the smallest bone in the human body, about {3 mm} long.
clue: A human thumb has 2 bones.

q: How much does the Liberty Bell in Philadelphia weigh?
hint: For scale: an adult man weighs about {80 kg}.
card: Its crack widened during an 1846 repair attempt, and the bell hasn't been properly rung since.
clue: A grand piano weighs about {450 kg}.

q: In what year was the Bastille stormed in Paris?
hint: For scale: the Great Fire of London was in 1666.
card: When the crowd stormed the fortress, it held only seven prisoners.
clue: The US Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.

q: In what year did the United States make the Louisiana Purchase from France?
hint: For scale: the US Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
card: The deal roughly doubled the size of the United States.
clue: Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo in 1815.

q: How tall was the Colossus of Rhodes, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World?
hint: For scale: a giraffe is about {5.5 m} tall.
card: It stood for only about 54 years before an earthquake toppled it in 226 BC.
clue: The Statue of Liberty's copper figure is about {46 m} tall, heel to torch.

q: How many hours did Charles Lindbergh's 1927 nonstop flight from New York to Paris take?
hint: For scale: a modern jet flies from New York to Paris in about 7 hours.
card: A fuel tank blocked his windshield, so Lindbergh had to look ahead through a periscope or out the side windows.
clue: Amelia Earhart's 1932 solo flight across the Atlantic took about 15 hours.

q: In what year did Leonardo da Vinci die?
hint: For scale: Columbus reached the Americas in 1492.
card: He spent his last years in France as a guest of King Francis I, with the Mona Lisa still in his possession.
clue: Michelangelo finished painting the Sistine Chapel ceiling in 1512.

q: For how many years did Pharaoh Ramesses II rule Egypt?
hint: For scale: Queen Victoria reigned for 63 years.
card: He fathered more than 100 children, and many of his sons died before he did.
clue: Louis XIV, France's longest-reigning king, ruled for 72 years.

q: On December 17, 1903, how far did Orville Wright's opening hop at Kitty Hawk cover?
hint: For scale: a city bus is about {12 m} long.
card: The whole flight was shorter than the wingspan of a Boeing 747.
clue: A basketball court is about {28 m} long.

q: What was the top speed of the Hindenburg airship?
hint: For scale: a cyclist rides at about {25 km/h}.
card: Its music salon had a lightweight aluminum grand piano, which was removed after a year to save weight.
clue: A car on a highway travels at about {100 km/h}.

q: How long is Royal Caribbean's cruise ship Symphony of the Seas?
hint: For scale: a soccer field is about {105 m} long.
card: It can carry more than 6,000 passengers, plus a crew of about 2,200.
clue: The Titanic was about {269 m} long.

q: How tall is a classic London Routemaster double-decker bus?
hint: For scale: a standard interior door is about {2 m} tall.
card: Routemasters ran in regular London service from 1956 until 2005.
clue: A giraffe can stand about {5.5 m} tall.

q: What is the wingspan of Howard Hughes's giant flying boat, the Spruce Goose?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 737 is about {40 m} long.
card: It flew only once, in 1947, about {21 m} above the water for roughly {1.6 km}.
clue: An Airbus A380's wings span about {80 m}.

q: In what year did the first commercial microwave oven go on sale?
hint: For scale: Ford started selling the Model T in 1908.
card: Engineer Percy Spencer got the idea when a radar set melted a candy bar in his pocket.
clue: The first jet airliner entered passenger service in 1952.

q: In what year was the first electric traffic signal installed, in Cleveland, Ohio?
hint: For scale: Karl Benz patented his Motorwagen in 1886.
card: London had a gas-lit traffic signal in 1868, but it exploded within a month.
clue: Ford started selling the Model T in 1908.

q: How much does a US nickel (five-cent coin) weigh?
hint: For scale: a US dollar bill weighs about {0.001 kg}.
card: Despite its name, a nickel is mostly copper: 75%, with just 25% nickel.
clue: A US penny weighs about {0.0025 kg}.

q: How wide is the Strait of Dover, the narrowest part of the English Channel?
hint: For scale: the Golden Gate Bridge's main span is about {1.3 km} long.
card: On a clear day, the white cliffs of Dover can be seen from the French coast.
clue: A marathon is about {42 km} long.

q: What is the surface area of Lake Superior, the largest of the Great Lakes?
hint: For scale: Wales covers about {20,800 sq km}.
card: It holds about 10% of the world's fresh surface water.
clue: Lake Victoria in Africa covers about {59,900 sq km}.

q: How deep is Loch Ness in Scotland at its deepest?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty is about {93 m} tall to the torch.
card: Loch Ness holds more fresh water than all the lakes of England and Wales combined.
clue: The Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.

q: How long is a standard US queen-size mattress?
hint: For scale: a sheet of letter paper is about {28 cm} long.
card: A US queen and king mattress are the same length; the king is just wider.
clue: A typical adult man is about {175 cm} tall.

q: How tall is Ben Nevis, the highest mountain in the British Isles?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.
card: Its summit is hidden in cloud on most days of the year.
clue: The Burj Khalifa is about {830 m} tall.

q: How many buttons are on a standard telephone keypad?
hint: For scale: a standard piano has 88 keys.
card: Phone keypads put 1-2-3 on the top row, while calculators put 7-8-9 there.
clue: A standard six-sided die has 6 faces.
